context.objective: Document how we carry out Quarterly Workbook Preparation & Binder, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: Thanks for sharing. Give me a moment to digest the file. Then I’ll follow up with a question.
The CSV lists building statement and lead-sheet support, running Check of Checks and clearing-account controls, then assembling binder support. Does that sequence reflect how this work is done today?

Yes, that order is right for those three, but they are from the middle and there are steps between them. After I build the statement and lead-sheet support, I record the quarter-specific accrual support, and only then run the Check of Checks and the clearing-account controls. After that comes the partner capital account and allocation checks, and then I assemble the binder support. I am the Fund Accountant and I do all of those.
What does the Check of Checks compare in the quarterly workbook?

It runs on the Check Sheet macro tab. I confirm there is an H-check or a V-check for every active general ledger account and that every check equals zero. In the same step I confirm the two clearing accounts, Other Payable 20090 and Investment Payable 20080, net to zero. Anything that is not zero I investigate and correct. I could not tell you the difference between an H-check and a V-check, that is not defined anywhere I know of.
What do you compare in the partner capital account and allocation checks?

On the M.1 tab I foot the first, the last and some randomly selected partner capital account samples and confirm the difference columns total zero. Then I confirm that investors with identical commitments have identical capital account and unfunded commitment balances. If they differ, either there is a documented reason in the governing terms, which I document and get reviewed, or the allocation gets corrected; the Controller and the client decide that as applicable, and it has to be resolved before the checks can be approved. I also review the distribution waterfall through the GP carried-interest step, and I send the independent recalculation requirements over to the FA-14 process. The Controller reviews these checks. How the random samples are picked and how many is not confirmed, I do not know that; it varies by fund. I should also give you the beginning, since I started in the middle. The whole thing starts when the quarterly close begins and current-period general ledger data and the client-approved method are available. First I review the limited partnership agreement and update the Activities and Tax Activities tabs: static fields, period-activity flags and tax fields. Every client-specific rule has to point to its governing document or approved source; if the method is unclear or conflicting I escalate to the Controller and the client. Second I copy the approved prior-quarter workbook and roll it forward, load the current trial balance, record the trial balance report run date and username, and confirm the correct entity and reporting period. If the entity, period or report source details cannot be confirmed, I stop. Third is the statement and lead-sheet build: I link the balance sheet, schedule of investments, income statement, partners capital and cash flow tabs to the trial balance, prepare lead sheets by account category, link each controlled balance to its source support instead of typing it in, and identify every active GL account that needs an H-check or V-check. Fourth, accruals: for Q1 to Q3 I calculate audit and tax accruals from the prior-year engagement letter only when that practice is approved, and in Q4 I true them up to the current engagement letters. If a letter is missing or there is an unusual component I get confirmation from the Controller and the client before going on.
Once you assemble the binder support, what happens to it next?

For the binder I collect engagement letters, DTM packages and transaction documents, as much as possible in advance of quarter-end, and route each record to its binder category in the digital binder. The reviewer, which is the Controller, has to confirm the binder is complete before the process continues. If support is missing I record it and escalate it; who is allowed to approve proceeding without it is not specified, so I do not know. After that is the last step: I complete my preparer review, then submit the workbook to the Controller, who reviews the workbook and checklist results and returns comments that I resolve. Then the Director does a final review, but only when the complexity of the close requires it. Then I run the File Cleanup macro, only on the copy that will go outside the firm, to remove sensitive internal data. I validate the cleaned copy, and if the macro changed required data, the approved file is restored and the change is investigated; the Controller decides that. The detailed validation steps after cleanup are not confirmed. Finally I hand off the reviewed workbook and validated external copy to statement production, FA-12, and the binder support to the binder process, FA-15A, and that is the end. One more rule: if anything in the workbook changes after the Check of Checks was run, the Check of Checks has to be regenerated, re-reviewed and re-signed. There is no documented deadline, and who formally approves the workbook is not confirmed.
What could happen if a workbook error is not caught before the reviewed workbook is handed off?
